title: Judge a staging by the text's words
statement: When learners judge which staging of a text convinces them, accept either choice but credit only a reason tied to the text's words, not lighting or camera alone.
detail: A 3D version shows one speech staged two ways and asks which staging convinces the learner more, and why, using one word the speaker says. Its marker counts a choice of either staging, or an argued blend, with a reason tied to the speech as secure, and a reason only about the lighting or camera, with no link to what is said, as partial. A secure answer then gets one push-back putting the case for the other staging, citing one word from the speech.
against: The task's student-facing lines are marked as the builders' own draft, pending approval (`othello-archive/src/content/oral.ts`, line 83).

evidence.quote: A reason that is only about the lighting or camera, with no link to what Othello says, is partial. Either choice can be secure.
export const STAGE_Q = 'Which staging convinces you more, and why? Use one word Othello says.'
